name: Banggai Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Peleng and labobo, in banggai islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A small brown owl with yellow eyes and feathered ear tufts. Note square head shape when tufts are not raised.

name: Monotonous Lark
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola to southern zambia, northern namibia, zimbabwe, and northern cape province
description: A medium-small, compact lark with a small bill, a plain face, and an indistinct eyebrow. It has streaky upperparts with a distinct rufous wing panel and a lightly-streaked buffy chest that separates the white throat from the pale belly.

name: Visayan Shama
rangeDescription: Philippines (ticao, masbate, panay, and negros)
description: A medium-sized, long-tailed bird of lowland and foothill forest in the western Visayas. Black on the upperparts and tail, with a white belly and pale pink legs.

name: St. Lucia Black Finch
rangeDescription: St. lucia (lesser antilles)
description: A small seed-eating species of forests with dense understory. Commonly found in pairs feeding on the ground.

name: Scarlet-headed Blackbird
rangeDescription: Marshes of northern bolivia (beni and santa cruz), paraguay, southern brazil, and northern argentina
description: A stunning blackbird with a sharply-pointed bill. The mostly black body contrasts with a bright orange-red head, breast, and thighs.

name: Bahama Woodstar
rangeDescription: Varied habitats in bahamas (except for inagua group) and the caicos islands
description: A small, long-tailed hummingbird of wooded and scrubby habitats including gardens; most often found feeding on flowers or at hummingbird feeders. Note the male’s iridescent purple throat and forehead and its long, forked tail.

name: Mayotte White-eye
rangeDescription: Mayotte island (comoros)
description: A small, sharp-billed warbler-like bird. Note the mostly yellow underparts, the broad chestnut flanks, and the bold white spectacles around the eye.

name: White-naped Seedeater
rangeDescription: Savanna of eastern colombia to southern venezuela and northwestern amazonian brazil
description: Large seedeater with a thick white bill. Males are black above and white below.

name: Snowy Owl
rangeDescription: Arctic circumpolar; irregular southern post-breeding irruptions
description: Otherworldly beautiful large owl. White with a variable amount of black markings; old males are the whitest, while immature females have the densest dark patterning.

name: Rennell Fantail
rangeDescription: Forest of rennell (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Mostly mouse-brown with a slightly paler throat and a russet wingbar. Long tail, often fanned, has pale fringes.

name: Whistling Warbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of st. vincent (lesser antilles)
description: A small charming inhabitant of woodland tangles and dense undergrowth. Plumage striking slate and white with a bold white eyering.

name: Yellow-browed Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds ural mountains eastward to sea of okhotsk, mongolia, and manchuria (and possibly northern korea); winters from nepal and bangladesh eastward to southern china, hainan, andaman islands, thailand, malay peninsula, and southeastern asia
description: Small, active warbler with greenish upperparts, white underparts, distinct pale yellowish eyebrow, and distinct pale wingbars (upper wingbar short and less distinct). Overlaps in range with many other warbler species; compare especially with Hume’s Warbler, Pallas’s Leaf Warbler, and Two-barred Warbler.

name: Samoan Myzomela
rangeDescription: Samoa (upolu, savai'i, and tutuila)
description: A small, strikingly plumaged myzomela with a bright crimson-red head, chest, back, and rump and black wings, belly, and tail. Thin bill decurved.

name: Eared Quetzal
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western mexico; occasional southeastern arizona
description: Scarce, large trogon of pine and pine-oak forests in mountains and canyons of northwest Mexico. Usually rather wary, flying long distances when disturbed, but can be found feeding quietly at fruiting trees.

name: Western Subalpine Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds in the western mediterranean (portugal eastward to northwestern italy) and morocco eastward to northwestern libya; winters in the western sahara, southward to senegal
description: A small, slim warbler with a long tail. Breeding males are distinctive, with gray upperparts contrasting with a puffy rufous throat and breast, and a bold white moustache mark.

name: Rufous-capped Spinetail
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Medium-sized, long-tailed spinetail found in the understory of humid forests often accompanying mixed-species flocks. Note the yellowish eyebrow, contrasting with dark cheeks, a pale throat, and a richly rufous crown, wings, and tail.

name: American Avocet
rangeDescription: Southern canada to northern mexico; winters southern usa to costa rica and cuba
description: Distinctive large shorebird with a long, thin, upturned bill. Look for bold black-and-white wings and long blue-gray legs.

name: Gold-fronted Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southern china (eastern sichuan and guangxi)
description: Small white-faced bird with a blotchy black cheek patch, a golden forehead, and black-and-yellow paneling on the wings. Passingly similar to Rufous-winged Fulvetta, which has a different facial pattern, a rich brick-red crown, and orange (not black-and-white) wing panels.

name: Black-crowned Monjita
rangeDescription: Southern argentina; winters to southern bolivia, paraguay, and far southern brazil
description: Large flycatcher of open grasslands. Usually easily detected, as it perched on top of fences, wires, bushes, and exposed branches of small trees, and sometimes forages on the ground.

name: Arabian Grosbeak
rangeDescription: Mountains of southwestern arabia
description: Handsome chunky gray-brown finch with a massive dark bill. Brown hood, white ear-patches, and brightly contrasting golden stripes in the dark wings and tail make this an easily recognizable species.
